o.text: From Old Anatolian Turkish ایكو (eygü, “good”), from Proto-Turkic *ed-gü (“good, excellent”), derived from Proto-Turkic *ed (“thing, goods”). Cognate with Turkish iyi, Turkish eyi (dialectal).
By surface analysis, ağırlaş- + -dır, from ağır.
Analyzable as tıxa- + -c. Cognate with Turkish tıkaç. Compare Turkmen dyky. The senses 'congestion' and 'traffic jam' are a semantic loan from Russian про́бка (próbka).
